newsitem.title: USA: Brazil external debt not affect money base-Loyola.
newsitem.headline: Brazil external debt not affect money base-Loyola.

text.p: Brazil's central bank president Gustavo Loyola said on Friday the Brazilian government's plan to use foreign borrowings to retire expensive domestic debt will not affect the country's monetary base.
"We take into consideration the monetary program," Loyola told Reuters before addressing a conference here. Loyola was referring on the government plan.
"We have to have distribution (of foreign borrowings) over a long period," he also said, adding Brazil will stick to its monetary targets.
He declined to specify the pace or amounts of foreign borrowings that will be used to retire domestic debt.
Brazil's domestic debt has expanded rapidly as the central bank sterilized enormous capital inflows.
Earlier this week, Loyola said the Brazilian central bank would use proceeds from an upcoming $750-million Yankee bond issue to retire domestic obligations.
